en: When sunlight hits a leaf, chlorophyll absorbs the light energy to convert water and carbon dioxide into glucose for food.
A chameleon changes its skin color to blend into its surroundings, which helps it hide from predators and sneak up on prey.
Stomach acid breaks down chewed food into a liquid mixture called chyme, allowing the small intestine to absorb essential nutrients into the bloodstream.
A caterpillar forms a protective chrysalis where its body completely reorganizes, emerging as a butterfly with wings to fly and drink nectar.
When a top predator like a wolf is removed from an ecosystem, herbivore populations explode and overconsume the available plant life.
The lungs transfer inhaled oxygen into the blood, and the heart pumps this oxygen-rich blood to deliver energy to all body cells.
Plant roots grow downward toward gravity to find water, while stems grow upward toward sunlight to maximize energy for photosynthesis.
A bear lowers its heart rate and body temperature during winter to conserve energy when food sources are scarce and frozen.
White blood cells identify and destroy invading bacteria in the bloodstream, producing antibodies that remember the germ to prevent future infections.
Fungi and bacteria break down dead leaves into rich soil nutrients, which living plants then absorb through their roots to grow.
Sensory neurons send electrical signals from the skin to the brain, which instantly processes the touch and triggers a muscle response.
Water evaporates from leaf pores into the air, creating a suction pull that draws more water and minerals up from the soil.
